summary: Codemasters' rally lineage from the Colin McRae Rally simulation series through the DiRT, DiRT Rally, and modern off-road entries.

entries.title: Colin McRae Rally

emulation.notes: Use native PC compatibility first; PlayStation emulation is an alternate preservation route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC output or PlayStation emulation upscaling

primary.why: The first Colin McRae Rally shipped on PlayStation and Windows, with a later 2D Game Boy Color adaptation. Windows has the highest fidelity ceiling for the original rally simulation and no sourced content loss compared with PlayStation.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release on a period PC or modern compatibility setup; use PlayStation emulation only if the PC version is impractical.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not confuse this 1998 game with the separate 2013 mobile/PC release of the same title.

entries.title: Colin McRae Rally 2.0

emulation.notes: Use PC for the main route; emulate PlayStation or GBA only for preservation comparison.

primary.why: Colin McRae Rally 2.0 was released for PlayStation, Windows, and Game Boy Advance. Windows provides the highest fidelity ceiling for the full rally content; the GBA version is a portable adaptation.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release on a period PC or compatibility setup; use PlayStation emulation as the easiest console-preservation fallback.

entries.remaster_caveats: The 2013 Colin McRae Rally reuses content from this game but is a separate, reduced modern release.

entries.title: Colin McRae Rally 3

emulation.notes: Use PC for the main route; console emulation is optional.

primary.why: Colin McRae Rally 3 shipped on PlayStation 2, Xbox, and Windows. The Windows release has the highest fidelity ceiling; the announced GameCube version was not released and is not treated as a playable route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release on a period PC or compatibility setup.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster is sourced; the cancelled GameCube version is not a playable release.

emulation.notes: Use PC first; console emulation is optional.

primary.why: Colin McRae Rally 04 released on PlayStation 2, Xbox, and Windows. Windows is the highest-fidelity route, with the same core championship/stage content sourced for the game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release on a period PC or modern compatibility setup.

entries.title: Colin McRae Rally 2005

emulation.emulator: Native PC / PCSX2 / xemu / PPSSPP / N-Gage preservation
emulation.notes: Use PC for the main playthrough; handheld/mobile emulation is optional archival work.

primary.why: Colin McRae Rally 2005 spans home consoles, PC, Mac, PSP, N-Gage, and J2ME. The Windows release is the highest-fidelity complete route for the full-size game, while handheld/mobile versions are adaptations with no sourced required exclusive content.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release on a period PC or compatibility setup; preserve PSP/N-Gage/mobile separately only for historical comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster is sourced; original online services have changed, with Xbox preservation relying on replacement services.

emulation.notes: Use PC first; console emulation is optional.

primary.why: Colin McRae: Dirt launched the DiRT era on Windows, Xbox 360, PlayStation 3, and Java ME. Windows is the highest-fidelity route for the full game; the Java ME version is a simplified mobile adaptation.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release on a compatible PC; use console versions only if PC access is impractical.

entries.title: Colin McRae: Dirt 2
entries.definitive_edition: Windows release plus optional Nintendo DS editor side route

emulation.emulator: Native PC / melonDS / RPCS3 / Xenia / Dolphin / PPSSPP
emulation.notes: Use PC for the main route; use DS emulation only for the unique editor/custom courses.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC output, with DS secondary limited to DS fidelity

primary.why: Dirt 2 spans HD consoles, PC, Mac, DS, Wii, and PSP. Windows is the highest-fidelity route and includes the full modern EGO-engine presentation. The Nintendo DS version is worth a secondary note because it is sourced with a track editor/custom course feature.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version for the main campaign; sample the Nintendo DS version separately only for its editor/custom-course angle if desired.

secondary.exclusive_content: DS-specific track editor/custom course creation in the Firebrand handheld version.
secondary.what_to_play: Try the DS editor/custom courses as a side route; do not replay the full career unless preserving the handheld version.
secondary.why: The DS feature is a sourced platform-specific difference, while the PC version remains the full-fidelity main playthrough.

entries.title: Dirt 3

emulation.notes: Use PC Complete Edition where legally available; console emulation is fallback preservation.

primary.why: Dirt 3 released on Windows, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, and later OS X. The Complete Edition bundles the game with its DLC tracks and vehicles, and Windows has the best fidelity ceiling.
primary.how_to_play: Play Dirt 3 Complete Edition on Windows if already owned or available from a legitimate key/disc source; otherwise use preserved console copies.

entries.remaster_caveats: Complete Edition was delisted from Steam in early 2017; legitimate access depends on existing ownership, keys, or physical copies.

entries.title: Dirt: Showdown

emulation.emulator: Native PC / RPCS3 / Xenia / arcade preservation
emulation.notes: Use PC offline content as the main route; arcade preservation is optional.

primary.why: Dirt: Showdown is an arcade-style spin-off released on Windows, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, OS X, Linux, and arcade hardware. Windows is the best-fidelity route for the home version, while the arcade release is a preservation curiosity with no sourced exclusive content requirement.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release if owned; expect online-server shutdowns and use offline/local content.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster is sourced; official online service is shut down.

entries.title: Colin McRae Rally

emulation.notes: Use PC for output quality; use mobile preservation if PC access is unavailable.

primary.version: 2014 PC port of the 2013 mobile release
primary.why: The 2013 Colin McRae Rally is a separate Unity-based release using content predominantly from Colin McRae Rally 2.0, first on iOS and later Android, OS X, and Windows. Windows has the highest output ceiling for this reduced modern release.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version if legally owned; otherwise preserve the iOS/Android release on compatible devices.

entries.remaster_caveats: Mobile-derived release with content predominantly taken from Rally 2.0; do not treat it as the definitive way to play Rally 2.0 itself.

entries.title: Dirt Rally

emulation.notes: No console emulation needed for the recommended route.

primary.why: Dirt Rally began on Windows Early Access and later released on PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Linux, and macOS. Windows has the highest fidelity ceiling and the earliest/full PC route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows/Steam release if owned; focus on offline rally content because official servers were shut down on November 8, 2025.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster is sourced; online-service availability changed after server shutdown.

emulation.notes: Use PC; console emulation is not needed.

primary.why: Dirt 4 released on PlayStation 4, Windows, Xbox One, Linux, and macOS. Windows offers the highest fidelity ceiling, with Linux/macOS as later Feral ports and no sourced exclusive content.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows/Steam release at high settings with a controller or wheel.

entries.title: Dirt Rally 2.0
entries.definitive_edition: Dirt Rally 2.0 Game of the Year Edition

emulation.notes: No console emulation needed for the recommended route.

primary.version: Game of the Year Edition / all-DLC PC release
primary.why: Dirt Rally 2.0 released on PlayStation 4, Windows, Xbox One, and Amazon Luna. The PC release has the highest fidelity ceiling, and the Game of the Year package is the most complete route because it includes the seasonal DLC and Colin McRae: Flat Out pack.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows Game of the Year/all-DLC release at high settings with a wheel if possible.

entries.remaster_caveats: No later remaster is sourced; use the all-DLC/GOTY package for completeness.

entries.title: Dirt 5
entries.definitive_edition: Windows release with owned DLC/Year One content

emulation.notes: No emulation needed for the recommended route.

primary.version: PC release with DLC/Year One content where owned
primary.why: Dirt 5 released across PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows, Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S, Stadia, and Amazon Luna. Windows has the highest scalable fidelity ceiling and no sourced content loss versus the console versions; cloud versions are convenience routes only.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows/Steam release at high settings; install owned DLC/Year One content for the fullest package.

entries.remaster_caveats: No later remaster is sourced; Stadia route is no longer practical after that service closure.
